name: Piram
title: King of Jarmuth
summary: Piram was the king of Jarmuth, one of the five Amorite kings who formed a coalition against Gibeon after the Gibeonites had made a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. He was defeated and killed by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: The Coalition Against Gibeon
keyEvents.description: Piram joined a coalition of five Amorite kings led by Adoni-Zedek, the king of Jerusalem, to attack Gibeon because the Gibeonites had made peace with Israel.

keyEvents.title: Gibeon's Cry for Help to Joshua
keyEvents.description: When the five kings besieged Gibeon, the Gibeonites sent a message to Joshua at Gilgal asking for help, since they had a covenant with Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Lord's Intervention and the Great Defeat
keyEvents.description: The Lord confused the Amorite armies, and Joshua defeated them with a great blow at Gibeon. The Lord also sent large hailstones upon them as they fled.

keyEvents.title: The Sun and Moon Stand Still
keyEvents.description: While pursuing the armies of the five Amorite kings, Joshua asked the Lord to make the sun and moon stand still, and God answered his prayer so that Israel could complete their victory.

keyEvents.title: The Five Kings Hide in a Cave at Makkedah
keyEvents.description: Jarmuth and the other four kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua ordered large stones to be rolled in front of the cave's entrance to keep them trapped.

keyEvents.title: The Execution of the Five Kings
keyEvents.description: After the enemies were defeated, the five kings, including Jarmuth, were brought out of the cave. Joshua had his commanders place their feet on the kings' necks, and then they were killed and hung on five trees.
